articles.title: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share, above projected range
articles.reason: 涵盖 AI product & news、Startup & business
articles.summary: The long-awaited IPO reportedly values the company at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
articles.full_text:
Anthropic has priced its long-awaited IPO at $83 per share , above its initial range of $70 to $78, signaling strong investor appetite for one of the companies at the center of the AI boom, despite market jitters following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which shook confidence in the industry.

The Claude maker sold 980 million shares in the offering, up from the 825 million initially planned, generating $81.3 billion in proceeds and surpassing SpaceX’s $75 billion record to become the largest IPO in history by proceeds raised.

At the IPO price, Anthropic is valued at roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, a significant increase from the $965 billion the company reached in May when it raised $65 billion in its last private market round , but below the $2 trillion it was reportedly aiming for several months ago.

Anthropic will begin its life as a public company on Thursday, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT.” A strong first day of trading would signal that investors remain optimistic about AI adoption, despite recent volatility in AI-driven stocks.

The company’s performance is expected to set expectations for private AI companies, including Anthropic’s main rival OpenAI, which was last reportedly valued at $1.25 billion but has yet to announce plans for an IPO.

Although none of Anthropic’s venture capital investors holds more than a 5% stake in the company, the IPO is a massive windfall for its numerous backers .

Investors who own approximately 1% of the company reportedly include Sequoia and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt.

Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC also holds about a 1% stake in the company, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Other backers set to make billions are Iconiq, Menlo Ventures, Coatue, and Sound Ventures, a firm launched by Guy Oseary and actor Ashton Kutcher, and Spark Ventures, the only VC firm known to hold a board seat at the company.

Some of the company’s existing investors, namely Sequoia, Iconiq, Lightspeed, Accel, and Altimeter Capital Management, are so enthusiastic about Anthropic’s future that they were reportedly planning to buy billions of dollars’ worth of the company’s shares in the IPO.   Yet the investors’ holdings in Anthropic pale in comparison to those of the Claude maker’s strategic partners , Amazon, which owns nearly 15% of the company, and Google, which holds almost 14%.

A group of major tech companies, including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners, have also agreed to purchase $26 billion worth of non-voting shares through a private placement alongside the IPO.

The company’s seven co-founders , including CEO Dario Amodei, each sold nearly 3.4 million shares in the IPO, according to the S-1 filing, bringing in about $282 million for each.

This post has been updated with the number of shares sold and IPO proceeds.

articles.title: Snapchat now lets developers build AR Lenses with AI assistants like Claude Code and Cursor
articles.reason: 涵盖 AI product & news、AI agent & application
articles.summary: Lens creators can describe the Lens they want in plain language, and their AI assistant handles the process from start to finish, Snapchat says.
articles.full_text:
Snapchat announced on Wednesday that it’s giving Lens creators the ability to build Lenses using the AI coding assistants they already use, like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.

Snapchat Lenses, which are a core part of the social network’s platform, are AR effects that let users alter their appearance, add digital objects to their surroundings, or interact with animated experiences through the camera.

The company is introducing Easy Lens CLI, which builds on its existing Easy Lens tool , which lets creators generate Lenses from a single prompt on the web and mobile.

Easy Lens CLI brings that same idea into developers’ existing workflows, allowing AI assistants to handle the technical work while creators focus on the vision for the Lens itself.

The launch indicates that Snapchat is looking to lower the barrier to creating AR content, while making its platform more accessible to developers who are increasingly using AI coding assistants.

Instead of requiring creators to learn how to use Snapchat’s own development tools, the company is bringing Lens creation into the AI coding workflows they already use, which could in turn expand the pool of people who build for Snapchat.

Developers enrolled in Snapchat’s Lens+ Payouts program can earn from the Lenses they create with Easy Lens CLI.

Snapchat says it paid out $1.8 million to Lens+ community creators last month.

Lens creators can describe the Lens they want in plain language, and their AI assistant handles the process from start to finish, Snapchat says.

That includes building with more than 100 AR building blocks and 50 AI asset generators, generating previews, and publishing them to Snapchat and tracking their performance.

With Easy Lens CLI, Snapchat says developers can create everything from Web Lens games with leaderboards to camera effects and beauty filters.

AI assistants can generate assets, build and test Lenses, address errors, and send updated versions directly to the creator’s phone.

The new capability can take a game from an initial idea to a published Lens in a single day, without developers having to write code themselves, Snapchat says.

The tool is aimed at different types of creators.

The company notes that game developers can bring existing browser games to Snapchat as Web Lenses, while AI creators can use assets from their preferred tools to build Lenses in their own style.

Additionally, agencies and brands can turn existing campaign videos, images, and other brand assets into AR experiences with less production time.

Easy Lens CLI runs on Mac, Windows, and Linux.

articles.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says it’s ‘hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen’
articles.reason: 涵盖 AI product & news、Startup & business
articles.summary: Nvidia founder and former CEO Jensen Huang stepped down last week amid several scandals, including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
articles.full_text:
The AI industry is entering a new era, and not just because of its constant stream of new model releases and discoveries.

The AI community must now push forward without one of its most influential figures, Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang.

Huang stepped down last week amid several scandals involving affairs with two employees and an alleged Chinese spy, raising potentially far-reaching national security concerns.

Speaking onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and President Greg Brockman each revealed that they had spoken privately with Huang as the embattled former CEO’s public image continued to unravel. “Jensen took one of the earliest big bets on us.

We took a big bet on Nvidia,” Altman said. “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.” OpenAI has worked closely with Huang over the years.

Nvidia invested $30 billion in the company earlier this year and designs the chips that power OpenAI’s technology.

Brockman added that he and his wife are friends with Huang’s family, so the couple had reached out “personally, just to be there for him and his family at this time.” “I think it’s obviously a tough time for everyone, but again, I think Nvidia is such an incredible company,” Brockman said. “I think that… what Jensen has built there, it clearly is built to last, and so we’re excited to keep partnering and looking to the future.” Huang’s impact on Nvidia and the broader AI industry has been so profound that nearly 200,000 people , including Elon Musk and other influential CEOs, have signed a petition calling for the chipmaker to reinstate him.

Nvidia executives said during the company’s earnings call on Tuesday that they do not have plans to reappoint Huang, even though the founder offered to return.

Altman was reticent to weigh in on Huang’s future at Nvidia.

When asked whether he thought Huang could return, Altman replied, “One thing I did not appreciate was everybody on Earth speculating with some random theory.” “I will say, I wish Jensen the best.

I wish Nvidia the best,” Altman said. “I don’t think the world needs another set of random opinions on what’s going to happen here.” Topics AI , greg brockman , Jensen Huang , nvidia , OpenAI , sam altman When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission .

articles.title: Satya Nadella predicts AI agents will reshuffle the economics of the web
articles.reason: 涵盖 AI agent & application、Startup & business
articles.summary: Microsoft's CEO says AI agents could disrupt advertising-driven business models, forcing companies like Amazon to rethink how they compete for customers.
articles.full_text:
In Brief Posted: 2:58 PM PST · November 18, 2026 Sarah Perez Satya Nadella predicts AI agents will reshuffle the economics of the web Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella predicts that the rise of AI agents is going to reshape the economics of the internet, impacting the business models of the companies that rely on advertising and what he referred to as “human web” traffic.

Speaking at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, the tech executive argued that the shift to an agentic web could change which companies pay others for traffic and for transactions, similar to how the transition from web portals like Yahoo to search engines like Google did years ago. “The current aggregators who have a business model which was for the human web will get, in some sense, reshuffled,” said Nadella. “And if you were monetizing ads because of the eyeballs, you now have to probably get down to essentially maybe CPC [cost-per-click] wins; maybe it’s more transactional,” he continued. “And so if you don’t accept the agent, somebody else will.” The discussion turned to Amazon and its decision to block AI agents from accessing its retail website, preventing them from browsing its catalog and making purchases on behalf of their users.

Nadella suggested that companies trying to protect their existing business models could lose out to others that are more willing to embrace the AI agents.

For instance, if Amazon continues blocking agents, another shopping platform such as Shopify, could allow them, and gain an advantage. “I think this is going to be interesting,” he said, speaking to the changing models. “It’s the same thing that’s happening in other categories, right?

Which is, if you’re in love with a particular business model, you have to kind of scramble,” he said.

articles.title: Felicis leads $7.5M bet on Unsiloed AI to make enterprise documents usable by AI agents
articles.reason: 涵盖 AI agent & application、Startup & business
articles.summary: With a team of just seven, Unsiloed AI plans to compete with tech giants and specialized startups in the crowded AI document-processing market.
articles.full_text:
As businesses increasingly turn to AI agents to automate work, the vast amounts of information locked in complex documents remain a challenge.

Unsiloed AI has raised $7.5 million in seed funding led by Felicis to tackle that problem, aiming to help enterprises make their documents more accessible to AI agents through specialized technology.

Silicon Valley venture capital firm Felicis led the round, with participation from Y Combinator, Orange Collective, and Uncorrelated Ventures.

Angel investors Aarthi Ramamurthy and Beth Turner also participated.

Business documents often include tables, charts, and complicated layouts that AI systems can struggle to interpret accurately.

But getting the information wrong can lead to costly mistakes for businesses, and the impact could be severe in the case of a bank, hospital, or a law firm, as they rely on these documents for their daily work.

Unsiloed aims to solve this problem with software that breaks down complex documents, extracts information from tables, charts, and other elements, and turns it into structured data that AI agents can use.

The technology also shows where the extracted information came from in the original document, so businesses can check the results rather than take the AI’s output at face value. “The problem with LLMs is they’re inherently probabilistic,” said Unsiloed co-founder and CEO Aman Mishra (pictured above, right) in an interview. “There is going to be some deviation induced.

There is going to be some hallucination involved, and that has a massive negative impact downstream.” Mishra co-founded Unsiloed with Adnan Abbas (pictured above, left), his former classmate at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur.

The two joined Y Combinator’s Fall 2025 batch after spending some time developing the technology.

Unsiloed is already working with customers in finance, legal services, and healthcare, Mishra told TechCrunch.

One bank is using its technology to process documents, while a law firm has deployed it on its own servers to handle contracts and old case files, he said, without naming either customer.

Mishra, however, named voice AI startup Bolna AI as a customer, saying it uses Unsiloed to ingest knowledge bases for building voice agents.

The San Francisco-headquartered startup has entered a market that is already crowded and includes specialized document-processing startups such as Reducto and Unstructured, as well as offerings from Microsoft and Amazon.

Businesses also sometimes use general-purpose AI models to extract information from documents, giving Unsiloed another set of competitors.

Mishra told TechCrunch that Unsiloed’s advantage lies in how it processes complex documents.

The startup uses what it calls “dual-stream” vision models, which handle text and image data separately, along with a technique called “heat map-based chunking” that helps identify the most important parts of a document. “In one of the streams you have the text tokens, in the other stream you have the exact image tokens,” Mishra said. “This is something that we have spent a lot of time architecting.” The technology then directs more computing power toward areas such as figures, numbers, and charts.

Unsiloed also uses a specialized decoder that takes industry-specific terminology into account, helping it distinguish between terms that can mean different things in different business contexts.

Supporting those claims, Mishra pointed to a test involving 542 financial documents supplied by an enterprise customer.

Unsiloed achieved 99.78% accuracy across roughly 84,000 extracted data points, per a technical brief shared by the startup.

The test compared Unsiloed with major AI models, Microsoft’s Azure Document Intelligence, and the customer’s in-house extraction tool.

The results have, however, not been independently verified.

Unsiloed also claims to have outperformed competing AI document-processing tools on olmOCR-Bench, a public benchmark developed by Allen AI.

In tests conducted by the startup, Unsiloed scored 88.0, compared with 66.0 for Reducto’s agentic system and 39.9 for Unstructured.

The benchmark covered 1,403 PDF pages and tested how well the systems handled tables, mathematical expressions, scanned documents, and complex layouts.

Unsiloed’s pricing, Mishra said, starts at one cent per page.

He asserted that the startup’s approach also helps keep its costs down by directing computing power toward the parts of a document that need the most attention, instead of processing every section in the same way.

Currently, Unsiloed has a headcount of seven people.

The startup, Mishra said, plans to use the fresh funding to hire more researchers and engineers, expand its sales efforts, and develop proprietary datasets to improve its technology.
